title: Outlook for Mac: DLP policy tips and override
notes: claim 53: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the Purview override path skips policy-tip selections that the cited procedure requires. The roadmap facts and off-by-default setting are supported, but the assertion that this feature adds no new data access is not documented.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy route runs through Customization, Policy Management, a policy configuration and Configure Settings to the named DLP policy-tip setting.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.
claims.fix: Use the fully documented creation route: 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook'. The overview supplies the wizard route and the existing docs URL supplies the final policy setting; retain both existing sources.

claims.claim: No documented PowerShell or Graph operation for configuring this Cloud Policy setting was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy service Microsoft 365 Apps policy configurations Microsoft Graph API PowerShell configure settings; Cloud Policy Graph API; Microsoft Graph officeCloudPolicies configure policy PowerShell. Opened Cloud Policy overview; no configuration call found.

claims.claim: The cited Purview procedure reaches Allow override from M365 services directly after User notifications.
claims.quote: Set the User notifications toggle to On. Select Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only). If already selected, uncheck the Allow override from M365 services option.
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom > Full directory > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User notifications > Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only) > Allow override from M365 services', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-osp-get-started. Retain the note identifying this as the oversharing procedure rather than a separate documented Mac dialog path.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule with Name, Policy, BlockAccess $true and NotifyAllowOverride WithJustification creates a DLP rule configured for override with justification.
claims.quote: Use the New-DlpComplianceRule to create data loss prevention (DLP) rules ... The NotifyAllowOverride parameter specifies the notification override options ... WithJustification: Allows overrides with justification.

claims.claim: WithoutJustification disables the justification buttons in the documented oversharing configuration.
claims.quote: "WithJustification" enables justification radio buttons, "WithoutJustification" disables them.

claims.claim: Learn describes NotifyAllowOverride values WithoutJustification, WithJustification and FalsePositives as requiring BlockAccess true.
claims.quote: If you set the NotifyAllowOverride action to WithoutJustification or WithJustification or FalsePositives, make sure BlockAccess is set to true and BlockAccessScope has appropriate value.
claims.fix: Replace this sentence with 'Learn says that for NotifyAllowOverride set to WithoutJustification or WithJustification, BlockAccess must be true and BlockAccessScope must have an appropriate value.' The notification page writes FalsePositives, but the cited New-DlpComplianceRule reference lists FalsePositive instead; removing the disputed value avoids teaching an invalid parameter value.
